FEN

Play a single game, a match against one opponent, or a bounded drill set. Turn on the coaching surfaces to learn, ask for a hint any time, and use Walkthrough, Scenarios and Progress to review what happened.

Choose promotion piece

New game

New match

A fixed series against one opponent. Colours alternate, adaptive difficulty stays off for the whole match, and the match stops early once the games left cannot change the result. Win 1, draw 0.5.

Drill

A set is a fixed block of cards, drawn up front with no repeats, scored on first attempts only; cards you miss come back once at the end of the set. Endless drill keeps dealing until you stop.

Import PGN or FEN

Paste a PGN game (tags optional) or a single FEN position. Input is validated; malformed or illegal input is rejected with a specific error.

Export

Opening library offline

Start with the main idea, compare both sides' plans, then study and practise the key decision. These are introductions to each family; use Explore for its variations.

Named lines include alternative and experimental play. A catalogue entry identifies a line; it is not a claim that every move is best.

The full catalogue is included in this file and works offline. Add more packs from your computer; they are merged into Explore and included in your saved data.

By default the opponent uses your personal opening lines. The full catalogue also contains uncommon and experimental gambits.

Add an opening line (INTAKE)

Moves in SAN from the start position. New entries are added unverified; only tick "verified" once you have checked a primary source.

Add a trap (INTAKE)

Provide the moves that reach the trap (SAN from start) or a trigger FEN, then the tempting bad move, why it fails, the correct move, and the refutation. Trap content is never auto-generated or auto-verified.

Export / import library JSON

Export your personal lines, traps and plans. Import replaces this personal library after validation; the included catalogue stays available. Use Opening packs to merge additional catalogues.

Scenarios

A scenario is a position plus a goal. Success is judged on the result you reach, not on playing one particular move, so there is more than one way to pass. The opponent never resigns during a run, because holding a lost position is sometimes the whole exercise.
